chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halaby, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who married a woman and touched her. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Her dower is obligatory, and she is prohibited to his father and his son.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a woman's dower and her prohibition to her husband's father and son after marriage and consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the intermediate legal status of a woman in a consummated marriage, establishing that her dower (mahr) is immediately obligatory upon the husband and that she becomes prohibited to his father and son. This ruling highlights the concept of 'haram al-tasbih' (prohibition due to marriage) in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing it from permanent prohibitions like mahram relationships, and underscores the financial and relational ties created by consummation.
